abstract: ABSTRACT Job losses (e.g., layoffs, furloughs) during the COVID‐19 pandemic were associated with higher levels of food hardship including food insufficiency, marginal food insufficiency, and difficulty affording food. However, we find the association between pandemic‐related job loss and food hardship was smaller in states with expanded Medicaid eligibility compared against job losses in states that did not expand Medicaid. Our key findings are larger among higher‐income households and childless adults–groups generally beyond Medicaid's core low‐income population, and they suggest that Medicaid's value as an antipoverty program complements other safety net programs during periods of unexpected material hardship.
abstract_zh: 摘要 新冠疫情期间的工作损失（如裁员、停职）与更高水平的食物困难相关，包括食物不足、边缘性食物不足及难以负担食物。然而，我们发现，在扩大医疗补助资格的各州，疫情相关的工作损失与食物困难之间的关联，相较于未扩大医疗补助的各州，其影响较小。我们的主要发现在较高收入家庭和无子女成年人群体中更为显著——这些群体通常超出医疗补助核心低收入人群范围，这表明医疗补助作为反贫困项目的价值，在意外物质困难时期与其他安全网项目相辅相成。
title: Unemployment‐Linked Food Hardships in Medicaid Expansion and Nonexpansion States During the COVID‐19 Pandemic
title_zh: 新冠疫情期间医疗补助扩展州与非扩展州的失业关联食品困境
